title: When Fresh Air Was Medicine
titleZh: 当新鲜空气被当作良药
paras: In the late nineteenth century, doctors often sent people with a serious lung illness to special country hospitals. They believed that fresh air, food and rest could help. These hospitals stood [[among|among]] trees, far from busy streets. A patient might leave a small city [[apartment|apartment]] and spend months there. Outside the bedroom window, there was often a garden or a green [[field|field]] where cows ate grass.

Life followed a slow daily plan. After a breakfast of eggs and [[toast|toast]], patients went outside. They lay on a long [[couch|couch]] under a roof, even in cold weather. Thick blankets kept them warm. Someone who could sit up might use an [[armchair|armchair]] instead. Talking was sometimes limited because rest was so important. At some hospitals, a visiting [[musician|musician]] played quiet music to make the long days more pleasant.

From the 1940s, new medicines began to change care for this illness. Many of the old hospitals have closed [[since|since]] that time. Some buildings now welcome visitors. A guided [[tour|tour]] can show the wide outdoor spaces where patients rested. Old photographs in [[online|online]] collections also tell this story. The empty chairs remind us of a time when getting well meant waiting through the seasons.
zh: 十九世纪末，医生常把患有严重肺病的人送到乡间的专门医院。他们相信，新鲜空气、食物和休息能有所帮助。这些医院坐落在树林中，远离繁忙的街道。病人可能离开城里的小公寓，在那里住上几个月。卧室窗外常常有一座花园，或是一片奶牛吃草的绿色牧场。
每天的生活都按照缓慢的节奏进行。早餐吃过鸡蛋和烤面包片后，病人们便到室外去。即使天气寒冷，他们也会躺在有顶棚遮挡的长沙发上。厚毯子让他们保持温暖。能够坐起来的人则可能改坐扶手椅。有时，说话也受到限制，因为休息非常重要。在一些医院，来访的乐手会演奏轻柔的音乐，让漫长的日子过得愉快一些。
从二十世纪四十年代起，新药开始改变这种疾病的治疗方式。自那以后，许多老医院陆续关闭。有些建筑如今向游客开放。跟随导览参观，人们可以看到病人当年休息的宽阔户外空间。网上藏品中的老照片也讲述着这段历史。那些空椅子提醒我们：曾经有一个时代，康复意味着在四季更替中等待。

q.s: Patients paid for their stay at the country hospitals.
q.why: 首段介绍住院情况，未说明病人是否付费。

q.s: Patients rested outdoors only when the weather was warm.
q.why: 第二段说即使天冷，病人也在室外躺着。

q.s: Old photographs online tell the story of these hospitals.
q.why: 末段明确说网上的老照片也讲述这段历史。
